status: frozen before querying any of the 141 member coordinates, seeing any member-level HSC candidate response, selecting a counterpart, applying a photometric quality cut, deriving a stellar mass, constructing a mass-current map, opening replacement-cluster lensing targets, or changing gravity physics
purpose: Acquire and hash every Hubble Source Catalog candidate around each published V19D spectroscopic member so that a later outcome-blind protocol can determine whether homogeneous physical member mass-current maps are supportable.

source.authority: Space Telescope Science Institute Hubble Source Catalog
source.release_choice: Use the documented, scriptable Catalogs.MAST v3 cone endpoint and freeze its raw responses. The acquisition does not mix releases or silently substitute v2 or a later catalog.
source.coordinate_frame: ICRS degrees from the V19D primary-paper catalogs
source.empty_cone_behavior: A valid HTTP-200 cone with no matches may have a zero-byte CSV body; retain and hash it as zero candidates.
source.pre_freeze_schema_check: A non-member 0.02-degree cone at the frozen Abell 2146 cluster center returned HTTP 200 with the exact requested header; no member-level cone was opened.

BULLET.radius_basis: The primary table records right ascension only to a whole time-second. At declination -56 degrees, half a time-second is about 4.2 arcsec on the sky; 6 arcsec contains the rounding footprint plus modest centroid uncertainty without using any HSC outcome.

ABELL2146.radius_basis: The primary table records both coordinates to 0.0001 degree. A 1-arcsec cone contains the coordinate-rounding footprint plus modest centroid uncertainty without using any HSC outcome.

outputs.per_member_payloads: one untouched CSV response and one exact query-URL text file per published member

gates.failure_rule: Fail before matching or mass inference. Do not enlarge a radius, change catalog release or magnitude type, drop an unmatched member, select a convenient candidate, or query lensing or inferred-halo products.

downstream_boundary.next_protocol: Freeze candidate association, photometric reliability, k-correction, stellar-population assumptions, and uncertainty propagation only after V19Y reports candidate coverage.
downstream_boundary.bullet_matching_warning: The 6-arcsec Bullet cones may contain multiple plausible counterparts because the published coordinates are coarse. A later protocol must use a preregistered positional and, where available, published-photometry likelihood rather than nearest-neighbor choice after inspecting outcomes.
downstream_boundary.mass_current_claim: HSC photometry can help estimate stellar mass but cannot supply transverse velocities. Even a successful match supports a projected rho-star times line-of-sight-velocity proxy with explicit projection uncertainty, not a complete four-dimensional current.
